title: SDK flightcheck mini-lab manifest (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience

Quick note: this is a compact, repeatable 15–25 minute hands-on mini-lab designed for engineers who need a minimal, high-confidence path from new repo -> instrumented sample call to Redwood. Goal is to give a ‘flightcheck’ that proves the SDK + local env + telemetry + fallback behavior all work for a first integration. Target audience: product engineers and platform engineers doing an initial prototype or POC.

Scope (what this lab validates)
- Local SDK install + sample app runs (JS and Python variants)
- Auth: local API key injection, env var fallback, and CI secret mock
- Network: basic call to Redwood hosted -> validate response shape and latency heuristics
- Telemetry: ensure request-level telemetry (latency, tokens, error codes) flows to our dev-stage observability pipeline
- Failure modes: simulate network blackhole, 429 throttles, model fallback to smaller quantized model
- Quick diagnostics: smoke logs, token-count mismatch detection, and KV-cache sanity check

Prereqs (what attendees should have before starting)
- Local Node v18+ (or Python 3.10+) installed
- Git + ability to run the sample repo locally
- Redwood dev API key (DEV-*) available or instructions to set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var
- Docker optional (for running an offline stub)

Session format (15–25 minute template)
- 0:00–1:30 — quick intro and objectives (what you will verify)
- 1:30–5:00 — clone repo, install deps, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var
- 5:00–10:00 — run sample request, inspect JSON response, confirm schema and latency metric present
- 10:00–15:00 — flip a failure flag (simulate 429 or drop) and observe fallback behavior + telemetry entry
- 15:00–20:00 — optional: run tracing snippets and check traces in dev console
- 20:00–25:00 — debrief, TODOs, and link to fuller onboarding docs

Runbook (commands & quick snippets)
- Clone: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-mini-labs.git && cd sdk-mini-labs/flightcheck
- Node quickstart: 
  - npm ci
  - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=DEV-xxxx
  - node examples/request.js  # prints tokens, latency, response.raw
- Python quickstart: 
  - python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
  - pip install -r requirements.txt
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY=DEV-xxxx python examples/request.py

Expected output (smoke checks)
- HTTP 200 with body containing: "model", "choices", "usage"
- Console prints: tokens_sent=<n>, tokens_received=<m>, latency_ms=<x>
- Telemetry event visible with tag: sdk.lab.flightcheck, env: dev-stage

Telemetry checklist (dev-stage)
- Ensure SDK sends an event for every request: event type = "sdk.request"
- Required fields: request_id, model, tokens_sent, tokens_received, latency_ms, status_code, client_version
- Verify minimum retention: logs + metrics for 7d in dev-stage; trace link to request_id present
- If telemetry is missing: check env var REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT and SDK feature flag TELEMETRY_OPT_IN

Failure-mode tests (quick toggles)
- 429 simulation: add header X-Simulate-Status:429 in request, expect SDK to retry once then trigger fallback route
- Network blackhole: run with REDWOOD_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:34567 and confirm client logs timeout and graceful error to user
- Model fallback: set PREFER_SMALL_MODEL=true and confirm selection of a quantized-v2 model in telemetry and response.model
- Invalid key: intentionally set REDWOOD_API_KEY=BAD and show clear error with code 401 and guidance on raising a support ticket

Observability checks (where to look)
- Dev console dashboard: /console/dev-stage/sdklabs (note: this is a dev-only view)
- Traces: look up by request_id in dev-tracing; spans include: sdk->http->runtime
- Quick grep: curl "https://dev-ops.internal/observability/search?q=sdk.lab.flightcheck+request_id:<id>" (internal only)

Developer ergonomics suggestions (ideas to include in core SDK)
- Single command: redwood lab flightcheck --key $REDWOOD_API_KEY (bundles all checks and prints a pass/fail summary)
- Human-friendly errors for auth/timeout/model-mismatch with remediation steps and links to support docs
- Local stub mode: redwood lab --stub to run an offline deterministic server that returns canned traces and telemetry events
- Telemetry dry-run flag: --telemetry-check to validate pipeline without sending production events

Common friction and notes to iterate on
- People frequently miss the env var name; consider supporting REDWOOD_KEY, API_KEY aliases
- Telemetry missing for users behind corp proxies; need guidance in the doc for proxy configuration and TLS root bundles
- CPU-bound local dev on M1 causes higher latency; add note about hardware expectations and sample latency ranges

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we want the single-command operator to be part of the SDK or a separate dev-tool? (decision needed by EngDX Q2 planning)
- CI gating: should the flightcheck be required in PR pipelines for any SDK client change? (minimal run + cached token required)
- Accessibility: add a short script that outputs an HTML report easily shared with nonengineers

Appendix: sample logs to expect (trimmed)
- INFO sdk.request request_id=abc123 model=redwood-compact-v1 tokens_sent=48 tokens_received=72 latency_ms=132 status=200
- WARN sdk.retry request_id=abc124 status=429 attempts=1 fallback=redwood-compact-quantized-v1
- ERROR sdk.auth request_id=abc125 status=401 msg="invalid api key" help="set REDWOOD_API_KEY or visit https://console.redwood.ai/account"

Notes to reviewer
- This is intentionally compact and biased toward a hands-on lab rather than a long-form tutorial. If approved, I will expand into a step-by-step doc with screenshots and the single-command helper script (prototype in PR linked above).
- Feedback requested on the minimal telemetry fieldset and whether traces should be included by default in dev-stage.

Quick links for collaborators
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1783
- Jira: ENGDX-412 (flightcheck minispec)
- Confluence: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGDX/pages/flightcheck-mini-lab

-- Asha P. (draft)
